title: Suvorexant and seizure timing
summary: Measure seizure risk within a defined vigilance state.

graph.evidence: REM sleep increased in Tsc1 mutant mice. The controlled seizure outcome was inconclusive.
graph.inference: Changing time in REM can change the overall event count.
graph.hypothesis: Orexin blockade might lower recurrence within matched vigilance states.
graph.experiment: Count EEG seizures per at-risk hour in each state at measured local exposure.

evidence: Estimated time in REM went from 5.4% to 8.2% at six weeks. The spontaneous seizure comparison gave p = .21 with 12–13 animals per treatment group.
inference: Reweighting published state-specific risks by sleep duration gave a central ratio of 1.03. The sensitivity interval crossed 1.
hypothesis: More time in a higher-risk state could mask a within-state benefit. The direction of the state effect in WWOX is unresolved.
experiment: Compare vehicle and suvorexant at common pre-onset state and time weights. Verify local exposure and preserved recruitment.
limits: Conditional research comparator. Pediatric neural exposure and WWOX seizure benefit remain unverified.
